precepts.text: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. That goes back to what we just read: this is when we became Greek citizens and worshiped idols. Everything Paul writes is referenced in the histories; Paul didn't just make stuff up. Where can we find it? In the book of Maccabees, which Esau conveniently took out, so our people in Christianity are lost and confused.
precepts.point: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God. Sometimes we take the laws of the Most High for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won't do nothing.
precepts.why:
Jason “forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.” He built a place of exercise, brought the chief young men under his subjection and made them wear a hat, the hat of Hermes. “Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners.” This is when we became Greek citizens, and we worshiped idols.

That is why Paul says: “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” That goes back to what we just read. We were led by Jason into heathenish manners and carried away unto dumb idols.

Everything Paul writes is referenced in the histories. Paul didn’t just make stuff up; it was based on something. Where in the Bible do we find it? In the book of Maccabees, which Esau conveniently took out, so our people in Christianity are lost and confused.

All you men that teach on the street must know this history. Verses 10 to 16 sum up what Paul constantly referenced when he said there is neither Jew nor Greek: we followed the Greeks’ customs so earnestly and desired to be like them in all things.

precepts.text: God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues. This is not contradicting Deuteronomy, because all men have different gifts. Helps and governments go back to the stewardship program; it all falls into place.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
The order Moses set in the camp continues in the church: “And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers, after that miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, diversities of tongues.”

The first leadership in the church is apostles, then prophets, then teachers. This is not contradicting Deuteronomy 1, because all men have different gifts. The wise and known men set over the tribes, and the apostles, prophets and teachers set in the church, are the same God's order.

“helps, governments, diversities of tongues”: that goes back to the stewardship program. It all falls into place. Every man has his gift and his place, and that structure is the order Paul rejoiced to behold in Colossians 2:5.

precepts.text: There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. There are not different ways, different types, or different forms of God and how to worship God, no matter what Oprah said. There is only one way, one truth: keeping the commandments and faith in his son. That is what brought us together. If fellowship or friendships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. There is no separatism in the body of Christ; we are all one.
precepts.point: Video played from the grassroots: it was only three families. No garments, little three piece suits, unleavened bread, lamb, bitter herbs, wine, and music from the families. This is what longevity and endurance look like. At one point the bishops would serve all the people at Passover; changes had to happen because of expansion and growth, and those changes were not comfortable, but they were necessary to bring us to where we are today.
precepts.why:
“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” A body has many parts that all work together: the heart that pumps blood, the brain that thinks, the arms and legs that move. We at Israel United in Christ are not many bodies. IUIC Austin, OKC, Atlanta and Arkansas are many members, but not different bodies. We are one body, in the same mind and the same spirit, so wherever you travel it should have the same feel and the same teachings.

Ephesians says it: “There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling; One Lord, one faith, one baptism, One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.”

There are not multiple ways, no matter what Oprah said. There are not different types or different forms of God and how to worship God. There is only one way, one truth, and to be in alignment with it you must do exactly what the body is supposed to do: keep the commandments and have faith in his Son.

That is what brought us together. If fellowship, friendships and relationships are what brought you here, you are in the wrong place. We are brothers and sisters who decided to do what God said against all odds and all the influences of the world; we don't care if you look at us funny.

We keep coming back to that soundness, that unity, that oneness in Christ. Anybody teaching anything other than that does not belong here. There is no separatism in the nation and no separatism in the body of Christ. We are all one.

precepts.text: For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office. The mind does not have the same function as the hand; the hand does not have the same function as the foot; but they all need each other. The body cannot function with all hands; if everybody comes in trying to be the feet, what happens? Disorder.
precepts.point: Each and every one of you has been gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation. For those who think you are insignificant: God called you in here, so you had better apply your gifts and talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God.
precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” God organizes the body, and God is who made us great. We are at the forefront, considered the vanguard, because God appointed us to be; if we move any differently than that, God will remove us and put somebody else there. Each of us was gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation.

Romans says the same: “For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”. Why do the members not have the same office? The heart and the brain function in different ways, but they come together to make the body function as one. The mind does not have the same function as the hand, and the hand does not have the same function as the foot. Every member functions, but they all need each other.

The body could not function with all hands or all elbows. If everybody comes in trying to be the hands, or everybody trying to be the feet, what will happen? Disorder. Everybody cannot be the head; everybody cannot be the shoulders. Everybody has their function.

So for those who think you are insignificant, just a regular Joe: God called you in here, and you have a mission and a purpose. You had better apply your gifts and your talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God. And preparing as a nation means more than food and water: we need lawyers, doctors, nurses, farmers. Go to school; master any skill, any trade, and bring that mastery back to benefit your nation.

precepts.text: Let all things be done decently and in order. The Lord is about order; he is not going to keep bringing the same member into the body. Can everybody be a teacher? Then who is going to read?
precepts.point: Each and every one of you has been gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation. For those who think you are insignificant: God called you in here, so you had better apply your gifts and talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God.
precepts.why:
God set the members in the body “as it hath pleased him”, and Paul says: “Let all things be done decently and in order.” The Lord is about order. He is not going to keep bringing the same member into the body, just hands and more hands; that is not how this works.

Understand how the scriptures use the body: it goes into functions. Can everybody be a teacher? Then who is going to read? Can everybody be the one for camp? Change is coming, because we have grown into a nation, and there are many talents and gifts, especially among the sisters, that have not even been tapped into yet.

We have looked at this from a war perspective, and it is all-out war outside; we need brothers prepared to spread this gospel. But in the functioning of this body, the Lord is showing that there are many more things we have to prepare ourselves for. If we don't, we will stay stagnant like others have. The camps that taught their people not to go to school, because Christ is coming soon, cannot open one building to this day, because they taught their people not to achieve greatness.

God brings the different members in for a purpose that all serves the same thing, with different functions. Back in 2016 the vision was set forth: Original Royalty, the kitchen, the school with the kids, security, video, music, all components of a society, the body of Israel under Christ working together for the common good of the whole nation. What was vision then is old news now; that is what order and vision do for a nation.

precepts.text: He gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for one goal. You see it in the teachers today: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage; each has his specialty, and you learn where to go glean from.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord is not the author of confusion; he is of order. When he brings in these different talents, gifts and members, he brings them for a purpose that serves one thing, with different functions. Paul shows it: “And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers”.

All of it was for one goal: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”. Though they had different offices and administrations, it was all for the perfecting of the saints.

You see it in the teachers today. Not all of them focus on the same things: some focus on prophecy, some on organization and structure, some on marriage, and you can see, that's his specialty. Learning from the deacons as the first internet member, you could see, he's good at this, I need some of that, and you learn where to go and what to glean.

What office can we say we don't need? If you think like that, you're not nation building; you haven't been given the vision. Back in the day some camps said, don't do anything with the videos, just play them. But the video needs music, an intro, something alluring, so someone outside the scriptures says, let me look at this, and once the scriptures start hitting: oh snap, I know who I am now. That effort is a member doing its part.

precepts.text: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. Shame on you if you come in here and sit on the talent God has given you. You have been given that gift for a reason: to utilize it and benefit your nation.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
Every member was set in the body for a reason, so Peter says: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.”

Shame on you if you come in here and sit on your hands, sit on the talent God has given you, and put forth no effort. If you have a craft or something to offer and you don't come in trying to show it and help, shame on you. You have been given that for a reason.

Your job is to utilize that gift and benefit your nation. Nobody should be bogging down your talents or making you stagnant; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching them to others where possible. That is being a good steward: the gift is ministered one to another, so the whole body is built up.

precepts.text: A man's gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men. When you have a talent, at least come in and say what you are able to do. Story told in class: when the OKC building was first acquired in 2017 it was in terrible shape, and brothers started coming out of the woodwork; a carpenter showed up, looked at the downed wires, and told them what was a fire hazard. The Lord brought those people in so they could build up the school, and after completion that brother disappeared: he served his purpose.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
“A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.” When you have a talent, when you're able to do something for the nation, at least come in and say, hey, I'm able to do this. We may say, all right brother, we'll utilize that gift a little later, or, we need you right here right now.

When the building in OKC was first acquired around 2017, it was trash. Out of nowhere brothers started coming out of the woodwork: I heard y'all teaching, I want to join. One saw them working on the building and said, I'm a carpenter, I build. It was dangerous in there, with downed wires, mold, asbestos and fiberglass floating; some brothers probably have lung damage to this day. He looked around and said, that's a fire hazard, you're going to die if you mess with that wire.

They were in there on the strength of the Lord, tearing down to build. The Lord brought those people in so they could build up the school. And right after completion that same brother disappeared: he served his purpose.

So a gift is not for hiding. It makes room for the man and brings him where the Lord wants him, and the body is built because every member brings what God gave him.

precepts.text: The parable of the talents: the man who hid his talent in the earth did nothing with the understanding God gave him, and his Lord called him a wicked and slothful servant, and said, take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security; realize that when you do not utilize that gift, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take this truth even further. If you cannot be used, you are useless; and none of you are useless, because we all have been called for a reason. There is something in you that you have to give to the nation.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
We have to utilize the gifts God gives us in this truth. A lot of you think your gift gives you job security. Realize that when you don't use it, God will take it from you and put the spirit on somebody else to take the truth even further. The parable of the talents shows it; the talent is money, standing for the understanding God bestows on you.

“Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth”. He hid that understanding, that gift, and did nothing with it.

Watch what Christ says: “Thou wicked and slothful servant”. “Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.” Even if you couldn't do anything else, you could have put it with the exchangers so something could be reaped. “Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents.”

We have seen it time and again: brothers and sisters with talents who hide them, or hold them over us: you can't do this without me. Know that yes, it can be done without you. If you can't be used, you are useless. But none of you are useless. We all have been called for a reason; there is something in you that you have to give to build the nation. The quicker we understand that, the quicker we get out of here.

precepts.text: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. We are all expendable and can be replaced if we do not put something into this truth. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices like they are less important. Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters that clean? Infested. Without the kitchen? Hungry. There is not one office we can say is more important; they all play a part. Even with leadership: a deacon is not better than you. I have to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. If you start to think you are better because of your office, this body is going to suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into rotation in the earth.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
God has given us different gifts and different offices but the same mission. So Paul says, “to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” We are all expendable; we can all be replaced if we don't put something into this truth.

What happens when someone thinks more highly than he ought? Just because you're the knuckle, the one who keeps us safe, you think you're better than everybody else. When members begin to think they are more important than another, dysfunction comes into the body, and members start treating other offices as less important.

Where would we be without security? Unsafe. Without the brothers and sisters who clean the toilets, the kitchen and the floors? Infested with roaches and mice. Without the kitchen? Hungry as hell; some single brothers look forward to the Sabbath because they get a real meal and not the peanut butter and jelly they're used to. The Lord brought all these administrations together so we can function. Not one is more important; they all play a part.

Even leadership. A deacon is not better than you; he could die tomorrow and be the devil. He has to keep the commandments and believe on Christ just like you. At the gas company nobody says, oh, that's Deacon; they say, nigga, I had to come shut your stuff off for you to come see me. No one cares. If you start to think you're better because of your office, this body will suffer. Respect the sisters changing diapers; respect the brother folding flyers, who in his tenure has probably put a million flyers into the earth, and it may have been you who got one.

precepts.text: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some security brothers, be careful: you get ahead of yourself ordering people around. That is your brother and your sister; deal with somebody like you want to be dealt with. No member is better than the next; we are all working toward the same goal, the kingdom. If we have this mind frame, we are going to move mountains.
precepts.point: Nobody should be bogging down your talents and gifts; we should be accentuating those gifts, furthering them, and teaching others those talents where possible.
precepts.why:
One body, many members, so “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.”

That striving spirit will unravel things, and people can see it when you move like that. Some of you security brothers, be careful. Because you're able to say move over here, move over there, you get ahead of yourself playing musical chairs: get up, go over here, no, sit right here, don't say nothing, hop on one leg, Simon says shut up. That's your brother; that's your sister. Deal with somebody the way you want to be dealt with.

Yes, some folks are hard-headed and act a straight fool, and sometimes you have to speak a certain way to let them know you're serious, because some don't understand organization. But no member is better than the next. We are all the same, working toward the same goal: we want the kingdom.

If we have this mind frame, esteeming each other better than ourselves, we are going to move mountains. That is what it means that the many members are yet but one body.

precepts.text: Be not ignorant of anything in a great matter or a small. You got to understand things in great matters as well as small. Do not be ignorant in the functionings of this body.
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.
precepts.why:
Paul opens, “Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant.” Sirach says the same: “Be not ignorant of any thing in a great matter or a small.” You have to learn this and understand it, in the great matters as well as the small.

Do not be ignorant in the functionings of this body. It is essential to understand how the body works: you have to realize what every individual is worth. Nobody is above this. You are special because you are part of the body, but do not think you are more than another part. We are all one, working towards the same goal, and we have to do exactly what the Lord told us to do to get where we need to get.

It is easy to come in, sit down, and think everybody is just doing what they do. But understand how intricate this thing is, how many different offices there are in this body. Some came in, got patted down, dropped the kids off, and did not think twice about how much goes into dealing with those children. Some will get a plate of food brought to them and have no idea how many hands were involved to make that plate possible. There are people with gifts to deal with things you do not even have to think about. Be not ignorant of that.

precepts.text: When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think; the scriptures are supposed to be inside you now. That you may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God: to prove means you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now. In the church you were ignorant, just walking along the line doing what everybody was doing: Christmas, birthdays, Mother's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, never asking why. Now everything has to make sense: what does the scripture say, where is that in the Bible?
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.
precepts.why:
To be not ignorant, Paul tells the Romans: “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. When you come into this truth you are supposed to transform the way you think. The scriptures are supposed to be inside you now, and you have to apply them.

And why? “that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.” To prove means you are not ignorant. It is the ability to process, to identify, to differentiate. Your antennas are up now, and you will not be ignorant in anything any longer.

You were ignorant in the church. You were dumb as hell, stupid, knowing nothing, just walking along the line doing what everybody was doing: it is Christmas time, it is somebody's birthday, Mother's Day, Father's Day, Easter, Thanksgiving, and never asking why. But now you are different. Now it has to make sense: what does the scripture say, where is that in the Bible? That is proving what is acceptable unto the Most High God, his perfect will.

precepts.text: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. The will of God, the laws of God: to process, to understand, to see clearly, bouncing things off of the scriptures. You no longer conform to this world; you do not move like everybody else anymore.
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.
precepts.why:
What is the will of the Lord? David answers: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God, and they are within the heart.

That is what a renewed mind does with them: it moves by them, processes, understands, knows, sees clearly. You have understanding now, and you are bouncing things off of the scriptures.

So you no longer conform to this world. You do not move like everybody else anymore. You are using your mind for what it is for: to delight in doing the will of God, with his law written within your heart. That is the opposite of the ignorance Paul warned the Corinthians about when he wrote, “I would not have you ignorant.”

precepts.text: You have one job on this earth: fear God and keep his commandments. You have been given a brain to understand how to fear God, what the commandments of God are, and how to apply the laws of God in your life. That is why you got a mind. If you are using your mind for anything else, filling it up with video game moves and the stats of every player, you are on that broad road to destruction. Fill your mind with thus saith the Lord: how do I deal with my wife, how do I deal with my kids, what can I do to become stronger so the Lord can use me?
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.
precepts.why:
You have one job on this earth, and you have been given a mind to do that job. Solomon gives it: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” One duty.

You have a brain to understand how to fear God. You have a brain to understand what the commandments of God are. You have a brain to apply the laws of God in your life. That is why you have a mind. Congratulations: you know the meaning of life now.

If you are doing anything else with your mind, you missed. You are on that broad road to destruction. You cannot fill your mind with kill moves on Mortal Kombat, the moves on the PlayStation, the stats of Kobe and whether the NBA finals are over. We don't give a damn about none of that. Fill your mind with thus saith the Lord. Apply it to what is necessary in life: How do I deal with my wife? How do I deal with my kids? What can I do to become stronger, a better asset in this truth, so the Lord can use me? That is what we are supposed to be concerned with. If you are concerned with something else, maybe this ain't you.

precepts.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied. If your mind is filled with games and sports statistics, that is where you are building your treasures, and all of that is going to be destroyed. Occupy your mind in the laws of God: how to unify, how can I be used as a tool for the Lord's army, how can I be utilized to push this truth further. That is laying up treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.
precepts.point: Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.
precepts.why:
Following what the Deacon brought out, Christ says: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” Wherever your treasure is, that is where your mind is going to be occupied.

If your mind is filled with Mortal Kombat moves and the stats of the greatest to ever play any sport, that is where your focus is and that is where you are building up your treasures. “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal”. All of those carnal things are going to be destroyed, so that should not be where your focus is.

“But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt”. When you occupy your mind in the laws of God, that is where you are laying up your treasure: how to unify, how can I be used as a tool for the Lord's army, how can I be utilized to push this truth further. That is where our minds should be: on treasure that cannot be corrupted, that no rust or moth can touch.

precepts.text: Think about the mind frame of a person that follows idols. Somebody created this thing, formed it, then turned around and said this is the god that brought you out of Egypt. Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach. You are on a fast track to destruction following dumb idols.
precepts.point: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. Why does he bring this up before what he is about to go over? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols' customs wanted instead of what the most high God wanted. To try to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult; you got to let them know, that is not us anymore, you got to renew your mind.
precepts.why:
“Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” Why does Paul bring this up before he goes over the order of the body? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols wanted instead of what the Most High God wanted. He tells the Ephesians the same: “remember, that ye being in time past Gentiles in the flesh”. That was us too: Hellenized, living like heathens.

Think about the mind frame of a person that follows idols. Habakkuk: “What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?” Somebody created this thing, formed it, and then turned around and said this is God, this is what brought you out of Egypt. You know how dumb you have to be? You stupid.

“Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach!” Woe is destruction: destruction to him that says to the wooden idol, wake up, and to the dumb stone, arise. You are on a highway to hell, a fast track to destruction, following dumb idols.

That is why Paul reminds them of the mindset they came from: to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult. You have to let them know, that is not us anymore. As Romans 12 says, you have to renew your mind. We do not conduct ourselves like that any longer; now we learn the order of the body of Christ.

precepts.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Stay away from it.
precepts.point: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. Why does he bring this up before what he is about to go over? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols' customs wanted instead of what the most high God wanted. To try to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult; you got to let them know, that is not us anymore, you got to renew your mind.
precepts.why:
Paul reminds the Corinthians where they came from: “Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” John gives the charge that goes with it: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Stay the heck away from them. Stay away from it.

This was us. Esau's successful mission was to make our nation forget the laws of God and change the ordinances, to take away our heritage and make us become something we are not. They created that mind frame here, and you see it amongst our people.

Once you come into the truth you are supposed to go ten times harder and repent, not go back to the idols you were carried away to. Habakkuk showed where the idol worshipper ends up: destruction, speaking to wood and dumb stone that cannot teach.

So Paul clears away the old idol mindset before he teaches the diversities of gifts, administrations and operations in the one body. Keep yourselves from idols, renew your mind, and you can learn the godly order the Most High set in his body.

precepts.text: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God. The gift comes from the Lord, and it is used to minister one to another. You have not been given a gift just for you. If you only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord. These gifts are supposed to be utilized for the building of the body; that is the stewardship.
precepts.point: All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.
precepts.why:
“But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” Everyone has a gift, but it goes toward the same goal in unison. It is not just for you. However the manifestation comes, there are different gifts given so that you can profit with all the nation.

Peter: “As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.” Where does the gift come from? The Lord. And what is it used for? To minister one to another.

You have not been given a gift just for you. If you have been given a gift and you only use it for yourself, it did not come from the Lord; it is not of the Lord. You are supposed to use that gift to benefit your nation and your people. That is why you were given it. If your gift only glorifies you, it is not about Christ; it is about you.

“as good stewards”: now you understand the stewardship program. These gifts are to be used for the building of the body, so that we can do what we need to do as a nation. The word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, all given “to every man to profit withal.”

precepts.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. How can I apply this gift to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? Some brothers had the gift of reaching people on the flyers: they can get a flyer into the hand of a man that just refused everybody else. You might have used that gift to hustle in the world, but that is not why you were given it. When your mind has been renewed you understand: God gave me that gift so I can get the word out. If you are not using the gift for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you. God gives these gifts with purpose.
precepts.point: All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.
precepts.why:
When you have these gifts, what do you do with them? Paul: “Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” How can I apply this gift to help somebody? How can I use what I know to help somebody else, to benefit my people, to benefit the school? What little brick can I put in that is going to bring us to where we need to be? That is the mind frame we must have when we function as a body.

Take the gift of reaching people. Some brothers can get a flyer into anybody's hand, even people who do not want one. The man walks off from one brother and tells him to go screw himself, and then another brother walks up the same way and the man leaves with a flyer in his hand saying, all right brothers, y'all take care. People have different gifts.

You might have used that gift in the world to hustle and get over on people, but that is not why you were given it. When you come into this truth and your mind is renewed, you understand: God gave me that gift so I can get the word out, relate to people, and show them thus saith the Lord.

If you are not using that gift for the Lord, the Lord did not give it to you; Satan gave it to you. God gives these gifts with purpose, “to profit withal”: every man looking on the things of others.

precepts.text: Whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; or ministry, let us wait on our ministry; or he that teacheth, on teaching. Everybody staying in their lane, working within the gift and skill set you have been given, not trying to force things that are not you. At camp, you cannot put the brother that is 105 pounds at the front sentry; he might be the fire teacher, or real good on flyers, but the wind will carry him off and we will not have a front sentry. When you operate outside your character, things get messy, and the person that should be in that position cannot operate the way the body needs, so we lack in different areas. Years ago a certain brother was put over the bills; one Sabbath the lights were off, and we learned that day he is not the one to put over the bills. We found where he belongs, and he is operating within his place now. Everybody does not belong everywhere.
precepts.point: All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.
precepts.why:
“Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”. These are the different gifts, administrations and operations. Whatever gift you have been given, if it is prophecy, prophesy with everything you have; whatever the Lord gave you, that is what you give.

“Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching”. Everybody stays in their lane. You work within the gift and skill set you have been given, and you do not try to force things that are not you. Size is not everything, but at camp you cannot put the brother who is 105 pounds at the front sentry. He might be the fire teacher, or real good on flyers, but if the wind blows it will carry him away and we will not have a front sentry.

When you are outside of your character, things get messy. If you pretend to be something you are not, you may be put in that position, and the person who should be there cannot operate the way the body needs, and we lack in different areas. Years ago a certain brother was put over the bills; one Sabbath the lights were off at the school. We learned that day he is not the one to put over the bills. We found where he belongs, and he is operating within his place now. Everybody does not belong everywhere.

“Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.” Everyone in their office, in their proper position. That is what Paul means when he says the one Spirit is “dividing to every man severally as he will.”

precepts.text: Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
“For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.” Precepts were called for from the brothers, and the first was Paul's own plea to the same Corinthians: “Now I beseech you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you”.

That fits the body. The members are many, but they speak the same thing, and there are no divisions among them. Diversity does not mean division: a different administration, dealing with something you don't deal with, is not separate from you. And different roles do not mean inequality; no function or operation in the body is unneeded.

That is why, wherever you travel among us, it should carry the same teachings: we are one body, in one mind, speaking the same thing. It all goes back to endeavouring to keep the unity, until we all come “unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ”.

precepts.text: Not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
The body is one and has many members, “so also is Christ.” Another brother brought Colossians: “And not holding the Head, from which all the body by joints and bands having nourishment ministered, and knit together, increaseth with the increase of God.” It takes some explaining, but it speaks to the same thing.

The body is held together from the Head, Christ. From him the whole body, joined and banded together, has nourishment ministered to it and is knit together, and so it increases with the increase of God. The members do not hold themselves together; they are knit together by holding the Head.

That is the unity of the body: every joint and band ministering what it has been given, all fastened to the Head. Not holding the Head is how a body falls apart, and holding him is how it grows. That is why the next scriptures read go straight to Christ as the head of the body, the church.

precepts.text: God hath put all things under Christ's feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, which is his body. Who is the church? Us.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
“so also is Christ”. How is the body Christ? Ephesians: “And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

God put all things under Christ's feet and gave him to be the head over all things to the church. Who is the head? Christ. Who is the body? The church. And who is the church? Us.

So when Paul says the many members are one body, “so also is Christ”, he means that we, the members, are his body, and he is the head over all of it. That is why there can be no division in the body: every member belongs to the same head, and the body is “the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

precepts.text: He is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: that in all things he might have the preeminence. Christ is the head of the body.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
Christ is the head of the body. Colossians: “And he is before all things, and by him all things consist. And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead; that in all things he might have the preeminence.”

Christ is before all things, and by him all things consist; everything holds together in him. He is the head of the body, the church, which is us. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead.

“that in all things he might have the preeminence”. The many members, with their different gifts, administrations and operations, are one body because they all come under one head, and he has the first place in everything. Make sure those precepts are written down: the body of 1 Corinthians 12 is the church, and Christ is its head.

precepts.text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both? There is no profit in hiding the gift or the administration that God has set you in. Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to push the truth and grow the unity God has called us to.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
The body has many members, and the different administrations in it are all to endeavour to keep the unity. So when we have these different administrations, we should not hide or neglect them. Sirach: “Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?”

That goes into wisdom, but also into the gift, because the wisdom God gives you comes through those gifts and through the spirit God puts on you. What profit is there in hiding wisdom or hoarding treasure? None. There is no profit in hiding the gift or the administration God has set you in and given you.

“Better is he that hideth his folly than a man that hideth his wisdom.” A man who hides his folly is better than one who hides his wisdom, who hoards up the understanding God has given him. If you know you are good at something and God has blessed you with that spirit, use it to keep pushing the truth and growing the unity God has called us to, because we are all one body and it all goes to the same Spirit.

precepts.text: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance. If baptism automatically meant water, why would John need to say I baptize you with water? Water baptism was John's administration, a tool to show forth repentance; it was never a requirement for the kingdom. He that cometh after me is mightier than I: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire. Did you hear anything about water? The baptism we must come under is through Christ.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
“For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body”. How many of us were dunked in water, the Baptist way? A church baptism in a green, filthy pond was shown, the brothers joking that it was pickle juice, but this verse is not talking about that. Baptized means cleanse. Write that down and look it up yourself: baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water, which is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

John says: “I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance”. If baptism always meant water, why would he need to say, I baptize you with water? It means, I cleanse you with water unto repentance. That was John's administration, water baptism, a tool to show forth repentance. It was never a requirement for the kingdom of heaven.

“but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear”. Somebody far mightier is coming, whose shoes John is not even worthy to hold. “he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire”. Did you hear anything about water? No. The baptism we must come under is through Christ: by one Spirit we are all cleansed into one body.

precepts.text: Says the same thing. You want the baptism of the spirit, because the fire is coming to clean up everything else. Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor; the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable. That is talking about judgment.
precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.
precepts.why:
Luke says the same thing, just in case anybody relapsed and wants to jump in the pickle juice: “I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire”. This is not talking about water.

“Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and will gather the wheat into his garner; but the chaff he will burn with fire unquenchable.” That is talking about judgment.

So you want the baptism of the Spirit, because the fire is coming to clean up everything else, and that is what Christ is coming with. The one Spirit that baptizes us into one body is the cleansing that gathers the wheat into his garner; the chaff that refuses it will be burned with fire unquenchable.

precepts.text: There are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all, and the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.
precepts.point: The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
The Lord filled Bezaleel “with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship”, gave Aholiab with him, and put wisdom “in the hearts of all that are wise hearted”. The Most High still works the same way.

“And there are diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.” To one “the word of wisdom”, to another “the word of knowledge”, to another faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, tongues and interpretation: “all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will.”

Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks and tech savvy. Those are diversities of operations of the same God, and all the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

precepts.text: The body is not one member, but many; the nation cannot be all teachers.
precepts.point: The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“For the body is not one member, but many.” The nation cannot be all teachers.

The tabernacle was not built by Moses alone; the Lord called Bezaleel to work in gold, silver, brass, stones and timber, gave Aholiab with him, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted. Today it is the same: carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks and the tech savvy are all members of the one body, and all the diverse gifts together build the work.

precepts.text: God hath set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.
precepts.point: The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

note.label: Exodus 31: Bezaleel and Aholiab, and the Sabbath Sign

precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” The Lord called Bezaleel by name and gave Aholiab with him; they did not appoint themselves.

So no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. The Most High sets every one in the body as it pleases him, the carpenter, the plumber, the electrician, the builder, the painter, the cook, and together the diverse gifts build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

precepts.text: The members of the body which seem to be more feeble are necessary; every part in the body has honor.
precepts.point: They set the ark upon a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove it, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals.

note.label: 2 Samuel 6: David Brings Up the Ark of God

precepts.why:
“Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.” Not everyone is a warrior, and not everyone goes to the front lines. But everyone in the body is important in some way.

“Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary.” The members that seem more feeble are needful, and on them more honor is bestowed. Every part in the body has honor.

So it was when David went up from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God. There were the chosen men, there were Uzzah and Ahio driving the new cart, and there was “all the house of Israel” playing before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets and cymbals. Every one had a part.

precepts.text: God set the members every one in the body as it pleased Him; promotion comes from the Most High, not from a man taking the seat himself.
precepts.point: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” Promotion comes from the Most High, not from a man taking the seat himself.

Absalom tried to take the seat, stealing the hearts of Israel at the gate and rising up against his own father. But God sets the members in the body as it pleases him, and he had not set Absalom on that throne. That is why the counsel that would have won it for him was defeated, and evil came upon Absalom instead.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

points: For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. A body is made of different parts that all work together: the heart that pumps blood, the brain that thinks, the arms and legs that move.

We here at Israel United in Christ are not many bodies. This is IUIC Austin; IUIC OKC, IUIC Atlanta, and IUIC Arkansas are in the building. We have many members, but they are not different bodies. We are one body, the same mind, the same spirit. Regardless of where you travel, it should have the same feel and the same teachings, because we are one.

Video played from the grassroots: it was only three families. No garments, little three piece suits, unleavened bread, lamb, bitter herbs, wine, and music from the families. This is what longevity and endurance look like. At one point the bishops would serve all the people at Passover; changes had to happen because of expansion and growth, and those changes were not comfortable, but they were necessary to bring us to where we are today.

But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him. God organizes the body; God is who made us great. The reason we are considered the vanguard is because God appointed us to be, and if we move any differently than that mindset, God will remove us and put somebody else there.

Each and every one of you has been gathered here for a purpose, brought into this body to benefit the nation. For those who think you are insignificant: God called you in here, so you had better apply your gifts and talents, because if you do anything other than that, you are going against God.

Preparation is not just food and water. We need lawyers, doctors, nurses, and farmers; that is how you prepare as a nation. So yes, go to school, get an education; do not listen to anybody saying Christ is coming soon so do not go to school. That is a bum mentality, and the same camps that taught their congregants not to prepare cannot open one building to this day, because they taught their people not to achieve greatness. You are the Israelites with the spirit of Christ on you: master any skill, any trade, and bring that mastery back to benefit your nation. Right now the biggest thing is AI: if you can go to school and learn AI, go do it. And brothers do not want to marry a sister with no aspirations either; we want sisters with that revolutionary mind to help her nation.

Video played from 2016, the Bishop teaching on this same chapter: all of those different members make up the nation. Original Royalty, the kitchen, the school with the kids, security, video, music: all of these things are components in a society, and the concept comes from this verse. The body is Israel under Christ; it involves different parts, but it all works together for the common good of the whole nation. An architect does not do what an electrician does, but when it comes to uniting for what they believe in, they all come out and support it. You might be good at filming, another brother at teaching; we are all linked together because we all keep these commandments, and when a brother falls low, we all support him. This was ten years ago; what was vision then is old news now, because that is what vision does for a nation.

For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews, those who grew up knowing who they were, or Gentiles, the diaspora scattered and calling ourselves by different names. That spirit is the laws and Christ; the spirit of this book called us into one body.

If the foot shall say, because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body? God gave you every member and every limb of your body for a reason. What part of your body do you not need? Lose your pinky toe and see if you walk the same. This passage is telling you that all of us were put in here for a reason and a purpose.

There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit; differences of administrations, but the same Lord; diversities of operations, but it is the same God which worketh all in all. Is that all talking about camp, camp, camp? No. We are so much more than that now: youth violence committees, Saving Sarah's Daughters, community cleanups, prison ministry, the colleges, music with Original Royalty, which now even has a modeling section. Back in the day we had two songs in rotation.

Wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, tongues: all the gifts are for the same purpose, the perfecting of the saints, to profit the ministry and build up the nation. You were not given the gift to hold on to it or keep it to yourself; you were given the gift so it could help somebody else.

1 Corinthians 12 is the embodiment of what a body takes in order to function. We would not be where we are right now if we did not understand that, but there is still more we got to put our brick in for to go to the next level.

Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant. When you read this, understand Paul is addressing the body; this is a letter to a congregation just like us. Imagine Paul writing to this school. It is essential to understand the functioning of the body: you got to realize what every individual is worth. You are special because you are part of the body, but do not think you are more than another part.

Wherefore I give you to understand, that no man speaking by the Spirit of God calleth Jesus accursed: and that no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost. By him actions are weighed. Somebody speaking of Christ and calling him accursed, that is not of the Lord; somebody who confessed Christ is Lord, this person believes.

Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. Why does he bring this up before what he is about to go over? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols' customs wanted instead of what the most high God wanted. To try to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult; you got to let them know, that is not us anymore, you got to renew your mind.

There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit. There are differences of administrations, but the same Lord. Definition read in class: administration refers to the organization, management, and supervision of the daily operations of a business, institution, or government; it involves coordinating people and resources to achieve specific goals.

There are diversities of operations. Definition read in class: operations refers to the daily behind the scenes processes, systems, and activities an organization uses. Administrations are the different offices that exist; operations are the inner workings, the processes that actually make the thing happen.

But it is the same God which worketh all in all. Different administrations and different operations all work for the same thing. Write this down: diversity does not mean division. Though it is a different administration, though it deals with something you do not deal with, it is not separate. And write this down as well: different roles do not mean inequality. We cannot look at any function, operation, or administration as though it is not needed. There is a reason why it is there. The body is alive because these administrations and operations function; it all works hand in hand, even the uncomely things.
But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal. Everyone has a gift, but it is going toward the same goal in unison. It is not just for you.

To one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom: these are the wise brothers that can tell you, if you do that, this is what is going to happen. How many times have we gone against wisdom and found out the hard way, wishing we would have listened? A hard head makes a soft behind. To another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit: some people have that retention, near photographic memory for where every scripture is. That is a gift.

To another faith by the same Spirit. There are people in the body whose faith benefits you. The Deacon got personal: when Bishop was going through his health battle, having lost his own mother to cancer, he was scared inside. Another Deacon looked him in the eye and said, you think the Lord is going to let him go this way right now? No. Have faith. That spirit of faith was for him too, so he would not be around Bishop with doom and gloom. Spirits like that drag everybody down; we got to keep each other in check.

All these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will. God has divided to every man as he wanted. Everyone has received something. New brothers and sisters, you are trying to discover what the Lord wants you to do here, because you woke up in this time period for a reason. What are you bringing to the table? How are you going to benefit your people and carry this truth to the next level? Sisters, the same: this is not just about the brothers, it is about a nation.
For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ. The brothers were asked for precepts, and they brought them.

For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

Name the functions of this body: security, kitchen, medical, maintenance, AV, the brothers that clean, hospitality, outreach, fundraising, the kids corner. Everybody is important. The brothers wiping the doorknobs saved you from a heap of trouble you never thought about. Take the kitchen out of here and the Sabbath feels completely different. Let all the kids sit in class and see if we can get through it. Different offices help this whole thing function.

The body is not one member, but many. If the foot shall say, because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; if the ear shall say, because I am not the eye, I am not of the body: if the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? God hath set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.

The eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you. Imagine somebody saying to another member, your job is not that important. You are not in the spirit of the Lord. Anything you remove, the whole body feels the change.

Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary. What seems feeble? The janitorial work, the kids corner, the offices that never get seen, like the brothers back there hitting the buttons on the screen; yet the buttons sometimes bring clarity to the class. When we are at camp and a point is made, everybody sounds off, and that makes a person really consider what was said. It may seem small, but nothing we do in this body is small; everything has a purpose.

Our uncomely parts have more abundant comeliness. The class named uncomely parts of the physical body, and the point stood: let the most uncomely part of your body close down and you will die within days. The uncomely parts make the world go round just like everything else. The counsel you give in secret is not for vainglory; you are truly trying to help somebody, and even though it is in secret, it matters, all the time.
But God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked: that there should be no schism in the body.

We talked about war, betrayal and family; now the unity of the brotherhood, which is very important now. There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit; differences of administrations, but the same Lord. The body is one and has many members. All of us play a part in the body of Christ, and in the end we are all one under Christ; that is the unity we have. Northern kingdom, southern kingdom, we all unify under Christ.

Video played, a black man on unity: that is why you all cannot get ahead, because you do not play as a team; you play as individuals. Even if you do not like something the group is going to do, you should play along with the team; that is team power. Wealth and power follow the numbers; if you are not pooling your money, your votes, your attention, your labor, other people will pick you clean and you will stay in the same spot. He is in the world and understands being a team player; some of you in the truth do not. You walk in here and try to challenge men who have been in this truth thirty years before you.

The members which seem to be more feeble are necessary. We do not all play the same part; some play a bigger part than others, but that does not mean you are not important. Cut one finger off a hand and you see the effect.

There should be no schism in the body, but the members should have the same care one for another. Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it. You are wearing a purple shirt; I am wearing a purple shirt. We are on the same team; you should not come against me and I should not come against you. That is what people in the world do; when you come into Israel there should be none of that, no I am going to do my own thing. We are all one under Christ.

Or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. Sisters, let that sink in. One of us wins, it is a win for us all; one of us is honored, it is an honor for us all. At my age this is the first time in my life I am in something bigger than me, fighting for something bigger than me; for the first time in my life I am somebody, and people treat me with respect. I grew up in a society where I never saw one black man honor another black man. When I came into this truth I saw men like Bishop Nathanyel, Bishop Canaan and Bishop Yaushua, men I could learn from and look at as my father. I grew up in a house with a father and did not learn a thing from him; I did not become a man until I came into IUIC. I did not know that when things get hard in a marriage you are supposed to stick with it and work it out; it takes a man to fix it and a little boy to walk away. I learned that from these men, and they did not just talk it, they showed me the example; they were living it. That is the type of men I want to honor. So you think I am going to listen to you and not honor that man? You have lost your mind.
Watch this. I know what the Christian is saying. They do not understand. They do not get it. But we are going to make sure that you get it today.
Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. Ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols.
How were you Gentiles? How did you used to be Gentiles? Gentile means nations. So there is no way that you used to be the nations and now you are not any more.
Who is this talking about? And who was carried away unto dumb idols? It is all going to make sense.
